account: Walsall Healthcare NHS Trust
description:
Hello,

Hope you are well.

Situation:

We have been experiencing issues relating to the connection between EMIS and our BD automated dispensing robot (BD Rowa VMax)

When dispensing, EMIS is constantly stating that it has lost connection with the Rowa, and is not dispensing products.

The interface receives the stock quantity etc, but then goes to 'Connection lost to Rowa'

We currently have a job logged with BD, but I also wanted to check if there was an issue from the EMIS side.

According to my colleagues, this has been happening since Wednesday. I was alerted to this on Friday 29th Aug, as we experienced an issue with connectivity on this day, this was escalated to the robot supplier.

Over the weekend that has just gone, my colleagues informed me that the issue also occurred.

On the 01/09, we experienced another connectivity issue with the robot.

Later on on the 01/09 (around 5pm), the same issue surfaced.

Could this please be looked into ASAP?

Thanks,

Brad
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hi Bradley,

As far as we are aware BD fixed this issue with Pyxis version 1.3.

From our logs we can see multiple logs of ''Invalid HL7 message format ExternalOrderId is not unique'. Our product team took this to BD and BD advised this issue had been fixed in version 1.3 of pyxis. I would advise on speaking to BD to see if there has been any changes or other known causes for this error.

A contact ( Liam Clayton ) from BD have also stated the following, from conversations we have had with them :

'The robot requires all message received from a pharmacy system to have a unique order ID for traceability purposes; you want to be able to search for an order based on, for example, its picking ticket number, and find exactly that order. So any order it receives that has a duplicate order number will be rejected. What I have seen in the message logs is that EMIS has begun to reuse order numbers. Looks like it hit a cap of 99999 (or some number of 9s I can't nail down the exact figure) and then reset to 1. It's then gradually built back up to reach the number it was on when we first went live, and so the robot has started to reject the "duplicates" which have become more and more as the number has risen.

The solution : I've run a script on your database to archive all previously used order numbers. They're all still there for audit purposes , but now have order number + date + ARCHIVE. So if you search a specific order number in PIC you will still be able to easily find and identify it, but if that order number is reused it will now not reject it.

Future proofing - I will ask one of my more technical colleagues to set this script up to run automatically every 6 months or so and re-archive all new orders in the same way so that if EMIS restarts reusing numbers again we are covered.'

Please enquire with BD whether the same is required for yourselves.

Thanks,

Azeem
